failure_summary: render_decision.zones.aliases['opp-key-square'] (spec c3r1) carries the board-false role 'a single square completing your opponent's four-in-a-row line' although opponentPunishment.kind='denial'/verdict='occupation' and its window c2r1-c5r1 is the PLAYER's line — on the engine's own finalMovestring 334332 the opponent's lone O at c3r1 completes no four — and run 1 echoed it verbatim as 'the square that finished their line' (A4 fabrication), while also never naming column 3 (A6) or the fork-creating move (A7c).
notes: n_runs=2 for this run (not 5), so no axis was sub-sampled away: A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 were graded on both runs. Board truth: decision=3343, afterBest=33432 shows X open three at display c3r1/c4r1/c5r1 with two gravity-top major threats at c2r1 and c6r1 and solver -18 for the mover, so the double threat both runs name is real and decisive (A3 pass both). G5 fail (both runs, render is byte-identical): the 'opp-key-square' role mislabels a denial/occupation square as an opponent completion — the generic '-key-square' role text at zoneAnnotations.mjs:124 is applied to half.completingCell without re-owning a denial half; current code re-owns it (a regenerated prompt now offers 'you-key-square' = 'a single square completing your four-in-a-row line'), so this defect is historical to the 08-06 record. A4 fail run 1: 'the square that finished their line' is false on 334332 (O has only c4r2,c4r3,c3r1; no four). A6 fail run 1 copied verbatim from the mechanical json ('prose never names column 3'). A7 fail run 1, subtest A7c: the mechanism is a fork and the fork-creating square (c3r1 = playing display column 3) is never named — run 1 says only 'the move that kept your double threat alive'; no '*-fork-pivot' handle was offered in the stored record (zoneAnnotations.mjs abstains when the pivot cell coincides with the other half's completing cell, which is exactly this board), so attribution is render/missing-handle, not purely model. Run 0 named it as '[zone:col3]column 3[/zone:col3]' and passes A7. A5 pass both after stripping tags: 2nd person, no field names, no raw coordinates, 'four-in-a-row line' / 'the key square' are allowed vocabulary; A5b N/A (player 1). G7 judgment pass both: every emitted handle wraps a phrase matching its OFFERED role (including run 1's false phrase, which matches the false role — charged once, at G5/A4), no over-wrapping, annotationRepairs empty, guardDiagnostics clean (servedExplanation == mechanism on both runs; the guard stripped nothing). G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard=null is correct by construction — renderReasonModel.mjs:336 only populates it when direction==='enabled_opponent' and this record is 'missed_own'. G4 pass: c3r1 verified on render_decision.finalMovestring 334332 (ply 6, mover 2); c2r1/c6r1 and window c2r1-c5r1 are afterBest objects verified on lostResource.finalMovestring 33432 and on the shown afterBest board. G3 pass: afterPlayed was omitted as tag-identical and neither run needed it. Not charged, but noted: BOTH runs omitted the required handle 'you-immediate' (c2r1), wrapping [zone:windows:c2r1,c6r1] instead — production's retry would have fired here (OI-183, unexercised by this harness).

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.zones.aliases['opp-key-square'].role (zoneAnnotations.mjs:124 generic '-key-square' role text, applied to a denial half's completingCell)
counterexamples.evidence: Role reads 'a single square completing your opponent's four-in-a-row line' for c3r1, but on the engine's own finalMovestring 334332 the opponent has O at c3r1,c4r2,c4r3 and completes no four there; the move is an occupation that denies the PLAYER's c2r1-c5r1 window (opponentPunishment.kind='denial', verdict='occupation', window=['c2r1','c3r1','c4r1','c5r1']). Run 1 served 'you let your opponent grab [zone:c3r1]the square that finished their line[/zone:c3r1]'.

The fork-creating square is c3r1 (display column 3, the best move), which coincides with opponentPunishment.completingCell, so zoneAnnotations.mjs abstains from offering the pivot handle. Run 1 therefore names no creating move at all; run 0 recovers only via the unrelated 'better-col' alias ([zone:col3]column 3).

grade_mechanical.mjs verdict 'A6: prose never names column 3'; served run-1 text names only [zone:col4]column 4, so the player is never told which move to play instead, even though bestCol=2 (display 3) is in the vector and offered as 'better-col'.
